gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, per the makers' own documents, the two 'lossless' paths on the Bose QC Ultra (2nd Gen) are conditional (aptX Adaptive lossless only with a Snapdragon Sound-certified source; USB-C wired audio capped at 16-bit/44.1 or 48 kHz), that Sony's WH-1000XM6 LE Audio/LC3 mode is Android-only and unavailable in the factory [Prioritize Sound Quality] setting until changed in the Sound Connect app, and that AirPods Max 2 need iOS/iPadOS 26.4 or later to pair, with Adaptive Audio, Voice Isolation and Siri requiring OS 26.4+.
standout_why: Compared against the cited SoundGuys best-list (states 'No USB listening' for Sony XM6, 'USB-C listening, aptX Lossless' for Bose, 'only SBC and AAC' plus 'USB-C audio' for AirPods Max 2) and the two cited What Hi-Fi pages (bodies truncated, could not be read). SoundGuys has the yes/no USB-C picture but not Bose's 16-bit/48 kHz ceiling, mislabels the Bluetooth codec as aptX Lossless where Bose's own page and press release say aptX Adaptive with lossless only on Snapdragon Sound-certified devices, and says nothing about the Sony LE Audio app-setting gate, the iPhone-gets-AAC-only point from Sony's help guide, or the iOS 26.4 floor for AirPods Max 2. ChatGPT's answer stated none of this. It refines the pick by phone platform rather than overturning it, so 2 not 3.
decides: Confirms Sony WH-1000XM6 as the pick for Android owners (LDAC over Classic Bluetooth, LC3/LE Audio once the app mode is switched). For iPhone owners it weakens the Sony case: Sony's own help guide says iPhone uses AAC, so the LDAC edge is nil, and the XM6 has no USB-C listening while the iPhone has no 3.5 mm jack. On an iPhone the wired-lossless options are Bose QC Ultra (2nd Gen) at 16-bit/44.1-48 kHz with the included USB-C cable, or AirPods Max 2 with the included USB-C cable, provided the iPhone runs iOS 26.4 or later. Bose's aptX Adaptive lossless is irrelevant on iPhone (Snapdragon Sound source required).

findings.label: USB-C wired audio format ceiling
findings.source_title: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) | Bose
findings.note: Bose product page: over USB-C with USB audio the headphones receive '16-bit, 44.1kHz or 48kHz from compatible source files'. Same figures in Bose press release. No 24-bit or 96 kHz path stated.

findings.label: Bluetooth lossless condition
findings.value: aptX Adaptive; lossless and low-latency only with Snapdragon Sound-certified devices
findings.source_title: Bose Unveils the Next Generation of the QuietComfort Ultra Headphones | Bose Pressroom
findings.note: Press release: aptX Adaptive 'allowing for automatic adaptation to lossless audio and low-latency processing when used with Snapdragon Sound-certified devices'. iPhones are not Snapdragon Sound devices. Product page FAQ: Gaming Mode also requires a Snapdragon Sound source.

findings.label: Bluetooth version and multipoint
findings.value: Bluetooth Core 5.4, two source devices simultaneously
findings.source_title: Bose Unveils the Next Generation of the QuietComfort Ultra Headphones | Bose Pressroom
findings.note: 'support Bluetooth Core 5.4 with multipoint connectivity' ... 'stay connected to two source devices simultaneously'. Product page lists profiles A2DP, HFP, AVRCP, BLE and 30 ft range.

findings.label: In-box cables (analog jack is 2.5 mm on the headphone side)
findings.value: 3.5 mm to 2.5 mm audio cable + 39 in USB-C to USB-C cable; no power adapter
findings.source_title: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) | Bose
findings.note: Bose lists '3.5 mm to 2.5 mm audio cable' and 'USB-C to USB-C cable (39 inches)'. A standard 3.5 mm-to-3.5 mm aux cable will not plug into the headphones directly.

findings.label: Price at bose.com
findings.source_title: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) | Bose
findings.note: Page shows 'Save $80 when you purchase by November 8, 2026'. Launch price $449 and on-sale date October 2, 2025 per Bose press release.

findings.label: Supported codecs by connection type
findings.value: Classic Audio (A2DP): SBC, AAC, LDAC; LE Audio: LC3
findings.note: Sony: 'AAC is mainly used in Apple products such as iPhone'. LDAC is Sony's codec at up to 990 kbps (96/48 kHz) or 909 kbps (88.2/44.1 kHz). Implication for iPhone: AAC only, no LDAC.

findings.label: LE Audio gate
findings.value: Not available in factory [Prioritize Sound Quality] mode; requires Sony | Sound Connect app set to [Low latency]
findings.note: 'In [Prioritize Sound Quality] (factory settings), LE Audio connection is not available.' GMAP gaming profile auto-switch also requires the smartphone to support GMAP.

findings.label: LE Audio platform and trade-off
findings.value: Android smartphones with LE Audio support only; lower connection stability than Classic Audio
findings.source_title: WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Pairing and connecting with an Android smartphone using LE Audio
findings.note: 'Both the Android smartphone and the headset must support LE Audio.' 'An LE Audio connection prioritizes low latency, resulting in a lower connection stability' and 'some of the headset functions cannot be used' while on LE Audio. Headset software and app must be updated to latest.

findings.label: Minimum OS to pair
findings.source_title: Connect and use your AirPods Max - Apple Support
findings.note: Footnote gives per-model minimums; 'AirPods Max 2: iOS or iPadOS 26.4 or later'. Page covers AirPods Max 1 (Lightning), AirPods Max 1 (USB-C) and AirPods Max 2.

findings.label: Lossless and ultra-low-latency audio path
findings.value: Wired USB-C only, included USB-C to USB-C cable, to iPhone/iPad/Mac with USB-C port
findings.source_title: Connect and use your AirPods Max - Apple Support
findings.note: 'You can listen to lossless audio and ultra-low latency audio with AirPods Max 1 (USB-C) and AirPods Max 2.' 'Use the included USB-C to USB-C cable to connect your AirPods Max to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac with a USB-C port.' Mac with USB-A: use a USB-C to USB-A cable. Apple spec page footnote: 'Lossless Audio listening requires a wired USB-C connection' and compatible content from supported apps.

findings.label: Analog wired listening
findings.value: Requires USB-C to 3.5 mm Audio Cable (not in the box)
findings.source_title: Connect and use your AirPods Max - Apple Support
findings.note: 'plug a USB-C to 3.5 mm Audio Cable into your AirPods Max 1 (USB-C) or your AirPods Max 2.' Apple spec page box contents list only 'USB-C Charge Cable', Smart Case and documentation (https://www.apple.com/airpods-max/specs/, read 2026-11-08).

findings.label: Feature requirements and non-Apple use
findings.value: Adaptive Audio, Voice Isolation, Siri need iOS/iPadOS/macOS 26.4+; non-Apple devices: Bluetooth headset, no Siri
findings.note: Spec page: works with 'non-Apple devices, but functionality may be limited'; Bluetooth 5.3. Apple user guide (https://support.apple.com/guide/airpods/pair-airpods-with-a-non-apple-device-dev499c9718b/web, read 2026-11-08): 'You can use AirPods as a Bluetooth headset with a non-Apple device' and 'You can't use Siri, but you can listen and talk.' Personalized Spatial Audio profile creation needs an iPhone with TrueDepth camera (apple.com/shop/buy-airpods/airpods-max footnote).

findings.label: Price at apple.com
findings.note: Same price in Blue, Purple, Midnight, Starlight, Orange. ChatGPT's $449 Walmart card is $100 below Apple's list.
